references.text: The Lord your God goes before you and will fight for you, just as he did in Egypt
Do not be afraid of them, for the Lord your God fights for you
The Lord your God goes with you to fight for you against your enemies and give you victory
The Lord fought for Israel by sending hail over the enemies
The Lord, the God of Israel, fought for Israel
The Lord your God himself has fought for you
One of you will chase a thousand into flight, for the Lord your God fights for you
The battle is not yours, but God's. You shall not fight, but stand still and see the salvation of the Lord
Our God will fight for us
Be still and know that I am God - an invitation to be quiet and let God act
In silence and trust your strength shall be
Jeremiah expands the principle that 'the Lord fights for you' from the nation of Israel to each individual believer/prophet.
Deuteronomy generalizes the principle from the Red Sea into a promise of victory in future conflicts.
